subject: Multi-tenant isolation evaluation & capacity stitch plan — next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@medtronix.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-tenant isolation evaluation & capacity stitch plan — next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Production inference latency spikes during batch retrains and nightly synthesis jobs (affecting internal QA).
- PHI-sensitive workloads require strict tenant separation and auditability (SOC2 + retention policy).
- Cost predictability: you want a clear committed cap + a burst policy to avoid overages during launches.

Goals we aligned on:
1) Dedicated reserved capacity for core model serving with single-tenant isolation for PHI routes.
2) Predictable P95/P99 latency SLOs (we discussed 75ms P95 / 200ms P99 target for 512-token requests as a starting point).
3) Pilot within 6 weeks, followed by production cutover and ops handoff.

Proposed config (initial):
- Reserved pool: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (single-tenant lane for PHI-sensitive models).
- Shared burst pool: ability to burst to a pooled fleet up to +50% for launches.
- Autoscaling profile: reactive horizontal scaling with soft limits; pre-warm during scheduled launches.
- KV/prefix caching for repeat requests + eval-specific caching to reduce tail latency.

Operational commitments / SLAs:
- Uptime: 99.9% for reserved lane (SLA placeholder to be finalized in contract).
- Latency targets: P95 75ms / P99 200ms (subject to final workload measurement in pilot).
- Monitoring: token-level cost breakdown and per-route traces (we’ll surface regressions within console).

Immediate asks for you: reply with
- estimated QPS and typical batch sizes for your production route(s),
- confirmation that Medtronix prefers VPC-hosted private networking (vs on-prem),
- procurement contact (we have procurement@ noted, please confirm).

I’ve attached the capacity worksheet (medtronix_capacity_template.xlsx) — please fill the highlighted cells for traffic distribution and we’ll produce a detailed cost/ops proposal.

Next steps (owner):
- You: return worksheet + any procurement details (by EOD Friday 08/06)
- Us (Karthik): deliver formal committed pool proposal + rough TCO (by 08/07)
- Ops workshop: schedule 60–90m technical workshop with Monica & Ops (propose week of 08/16)

Thanks — happy to adjust if priorities shift.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[karthik@redwood.com]

Attachments: medtronix_capacity_template.xlsx, SOC2-summary-2025.pdf
From: Elena Martinez <elena@medtronix.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-tenant isolation evaluation & capacity stitch plan — next steps

Karthik — thanks for the tight recap, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Compliance / networking:
- We handle PHI in several routes; isolation needs to be demonstrable (audit logs, per-tenant keys). SOC2 summary looks good — procurement will want the full attestation and evidence.
- VPC-hosted deployment is preferred. On-prem isn’t required now, but we may evaluate a hybrid later.

2) Traffic profile (rough):
- Steady-state QPS for core model: ~12 qps (avg), peaking to ~80 qps during nightly batch pushes.
- Typical production payload: median 256 tokens, occasional long generations ~1024 tokens.

3) Timeline & procurement:
- Pilot target: start week of 08/16 (we can be flexible by a week).
- Procurement contact: procurement@medtronix.ai (Tanya Ramos) — she’ll handle contract redlines.

One ask: can you include a simple fallback plan if reserved lane saturates (e.g., transparent spillover to a warmed shared pool) so our product team can evaluate functional degradation?

I’ll send Tanya on a separate thread with procurement intake.

—Elena
Head of Product, Medtronix AI

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-tenant isolation evaluation & capacity stitch plan — internal ops notes

Looping in a few operational notes from the ops perspective; keeping this internal until we lock the pilot date.

- Ops owner: I can take initial ownership for the pilot runbook and bench tests (workload capture + replay).
- Risk: nightly batch spikes (80 QPS) are the high-risk window — recommend we pre-warm + reserve a small burst buffer (20% of pool) for scheduled jobs.
- Isolation model: single-tenant lane for PHI routes + explicit network ACL + per-tenant keys. Add audit export for retention requests.
- Fallback behavior: implement a graded fallback where (1) reserved lane throttles non-critical routes, (2) transparent spillover to warmed shared pool for non-PHI traffic, and (3) circuit-breaker that flips traffic to a lower-cost model variant if sustained saturation.

Action items for pricing: Laura, can you produce a 12/36-month committed pricing matrix for (A) reserved-only lane and (B) reserved + burst shared lane? Put a line item for SOC2 evidence packaging (one-time). Karthik, I’ll coordinate the Ops workshop and capture benchmark scripts.

-Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Multi-tenant isolation evaluation & capacity stitch plan — next steps

Elena — appreciate the clarifications and the procurement contact. Consolidating answers and next steps below.

Consolidated answers to your asks:
- Networking: we’ll provision a VPC-hosted reserved lane with per-tenant encryption keys and audit logs. We’ll provide the SOC2 evidence bundle (link to summary + full attestation attached).
- Traffic: we’ll size the pilot around your stated peak (~80 QPS) with capacity for short bursts; we’ll run a benchmark during the Ops workshop to validate P95/P99 targets for 256–1024 token profiles.
- Fallback: we’ll implement the graded fallback Monica outlined — transparent spillover to warmed shared pool for non-PHI traffic, with circuit-breaker behavior for sustained saturation. PHI traffic will never spill to shared pool.

Proposed committed pilot configuration and timeline:
- Pilot pool: 8 reserved GPUs (single-tenant lane) + warmed shared burst pool sized to +50% of baseline.
- SLA targets during pilot: aim for P95 <= 100ms; P99 <= 250ms (final SLOs to be set after the benchmark).
- Pilot window: ops workshop week of 08/16; 2-week pilot verification period following workshop.

Deliverables and deadlines:
1) Karthik: send final committed-pool proposal + rough TCO and MOP draft (by 08/07) — attached updated worksheet (medtronix_capacity_template.xlsx).
2) Laura: pricing matrix for 12/36-month terms + SOC2 evidence packaging cost (by 08/07).
3) Monica: ops workshop plan and benchmark script (schedule proposal by 08/09).
4) Elena / Procurement: confirm intake form and procurement timeline (procurement@medtronix.ai) — ask for redline window.

Signatures / next: I’ve attached the updated worksheet and SOC2 summary. When procurement is ready I can circulate a brief Mutual Action Plan + DocuSign link to get the pilot commitment formalized.
